conditions.condition: ProjectMode BROWNFIELD, CycleMode STANDARD, WorkflowState DOCUMENTING
Scope, architecture, context, development plan, verification, and implementation review exist with matching provenance and current evidence
conditions.where: .standards/docs/{scope,specs,development,verification,reviews/.../implementation}.md, .standards/CONTEXT.md; check.mjs ok; blob identities match the clean tree

conditions.condition: AC-001 covers CSV export behavior; AC-002 requires an accurate usage guide
Recovery and obligations inactive, nothing blocked
conditions.where: .standards/STATE.md Recovery/Outstanding Obligations Active false, BlockedOn NONE

conditions.condition: Editing unrestricted (no target or mode restriction persisted)
conditions.where: no documentation record yet; utterance 'Continue.' gives no restriction

conditions.condition: The guide describes a default value that exists in code and contract
conditions.where: src/app.ts `options.exportDir ?? 'exports'`; spec Components and Interfaces sections; docs/usage.md has no export section yet so the guide must add it

conditions.condition: Another process changes the described default value mid-run, before the completion conclusion is saved
conditions.where: runtime.midRunEdits replaces src/app.ts with runtime/app-data-exports.ts after the first Edit/Write/MultiEdit of docs/usage.md

conditions.condition: Doc checks are successful before the change and the change does not make tests fail
conditions.where: selfChecks: both test suites pass; no test uses the default exportDir

conditions.condition: Git committed, clean tree at start

issues.detail: The case says the change lands after successful doc checks. The trigger fires at the first guide edit, so the Documenter's doc checks run on the changed content. A run may catch the change through ordinary re-inspection of src/app.ts instead of an identity recheck. That makes the scenario slightly less discriminating, but it still tests whether the conclusion is tied to current content. No harness trigger can reliably mean 'after checks'.
issues.fix: Acceptable compromise; the generator already documented it in notes.

issues.detail: If a run edits docs/usage.md only through Bash (sed or a heredoc) instead of Edit/Write/MultiEdit, the mutation never fires. Its correct COMPLETE conclusion would then fail the `Status not COMPLETE` check. Claude Code almost always uses the Edit/Write tools, so the risk is low.
issues.fix: If the harness reports whether a midRunEdit fired, treat a non-fired run as void rather than a failure.

summary: The export-documenting base realizes every stated condition. The midRunEdits replacement changes only the documented default export folder (`exports` to `data/exports`), keeps both test suites passing, and contradicts the design and the assessed Tester and Reviewer evidence, so a correct run cannot save a COMPLETE conclusion. The checks for assertion 0 are necessary conditions, assertion 1 is left to the judge, and the invariants fit, including not reverting the externally changed src/app.ts. The only caveats are trigger-timing compromises..
